title: They rejected the Reminder, and it is a mighty Book.
subtitle: A protected book no one can match
then: Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi and Qatadah said the Reminder here {idea}is the Quran.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}protected and preserved, and nobody can produce anything like it.{/idea} Quraysh rejected it, but rejection did nothing to its standing.
now: A book has sat on your shelf for years, the cover dusty. You meant to read it properly. {idea}It has not lost anything by waiting.{/idea} The only one missing out is the person who keeps not opening it.
old: If I ignore the Quran, it does not really matter much.
new: The Quran stays mighty whether I read it or not. Ignoring it only costs me.
try: Open a physical or digital mushaf today and read one page.

title: Falsehood cannot reach it from front or back.
subtitle: Sent down by the Wise, the Praiseworthy
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}there is no way to corrupt it{/idea}, because it came from the Lord of the worlds. He is Wise in all He says and does, and {reward}Praiseworthy in all He commands and forbids.{/reward}
now: Your feed shows a story, then a correction, then a correction of the correction. Edited photos, rewritten history, deleted posts. {reward}In all that noise, there is one text that falsehood cannot get into.{/reward}
old: Everything is spin; nothing I read can be fully trusted.
new: The Quran is guarded from falsehood on every side. I can rest my trust there.
try: Replace five minutes of news scrolling today with five minutes of Quran.

title: Every insult you hear, messengers before you heard too.
subtitle: Comfort for the rejected, and a Lord of forgiveness
then: Qatadah and As-Suddi said: {idea}nothing is said to you by way of rejection that was not said to the messengers before you.{/idea} As they bore insults with patience, so must you. Then a balance: your Lord {reward}forgives those who turn to Him{/reward}, and punishes those who persist.
now: You try to do the right thing and someone mocks you for it. A family member calls you extreme for praying on time. {idea}You are not the first. You are walking an old road.{/idea}
old: If people mock me for my faith, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Mockery for doing right is an old pattern. Messengers faced it, and patience is the answer.
try: The next time someone mocks a good habit of yours, answer calmly and keep doing it.

title: For believers, guidance and cure; for others, a distant call.
subtitle: The same words, two very different effects
then: Ibn Kathir says their rejection was {trap}the disbelief of stubbornness.{/trap} Had it come in a foreign language, they would have complained it was not Arabic. For a believer it is {reward}guidance for the heart and a cure for doubts.{/reward} Mujahid said the distant place is far from their hearts.
now: Two people sit through the same Friday talk. One leaves lighter, a doubt settled. The other says it was too long. {idea}The words were the same. The hearts were not.{/idea}
old: If the reminder were delivered better, it would reach me.
new: The Quran heals the heart that comes to it in faith. Distance is in the listener, not the words.
try: Bring one real doubt or worry to the Quran today and read a passage with it in mind.

title: Musa's people argued over their book too.
subtitle: A delay that is a mercy, not a forgetting
then: Ibn Kathir says Musa's people {trap}disputed his Scripture and showed him no respect{/trap}, just as Quraysh did with the Prophet ﷺ. Had a word not gone before from Allah, {idea}delaying the reckoning to an appointed term{/idea}, it would have been settled already.
now: You did something wrong and nothing happened. A week passed, then a month. {trap}It is easy to think it did not matter.{/trap} {idea}The delay is time given, not a sign that no one noticed.{/idea}
old: If nothing bad happened after I did wrong, it must not have mattered.
new: Allah's delay is a mercy with a deadline. It is space for me to turn back.
try: Think of one wrong that seemed to have no consequence, and seek forgiveness for it today.

title: Your good is for you, your harm is against you.
subtitle: And your Lord is never unjust
then: Ibn Kathir says the benefit of a good deed {reward}comes back to the one who did it{/reward}, and so do the consequences of evil. Allah {idea}punishes no one except after establishing proof and sending a messenger.{/idea}
now: You hold the door for a stranger, help your kid with homework, pray when you are tired. It feels like giving away. {reward}It is all landing in your own account.{/reward} So is the sharp reply you send at midnight.
old: When I do good, I am mostly doing it for others.
new: Every good deed is a gift to my own soul, and every harm I do lands on me too.
try: Do one good deed today and quietly remind yourself it is for your own soul.

title: He knows the Hour, every fruit, every birth.
subtitle: Nothing grows or is born outside His knowledge
then: When Jibril asked about the Hour, the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}the one asked knows no more than the one asking.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that every fruit from its sheath and every pregnancy is in His knowledge. On the Day, those who worshipped others will say {trap}none of us bears witness to any partner.{/trap}
now: You are waiting outside a delivery room, or for test results, or for a harvest of a different kind: a job offer, an answer. {idea}He already knows every detail of what is coming.{/idea} You can hand Him the waiting.
old: I need to know what is coming before I can feel calm.
new: He knows every birth, every fruit, every hour. My calm can rest on His knowing.
try: Name one thing you are anxiously waiting for and give it to Allah in a short dua.

title: What they called on before simply disappears.
subtitle: False supports leave when you need them
then: Ibn Kathir says those they used to invoke {trap}will go away and be of no benefit to them.{/trap} The idolators of Makkah trusted their idols to intercede. On the Day, there would be no refuge from what they had done.
now: You lean on a habit to cope: a show, a snack, a scroll. It is there every night. {trap}Then the real crisis comes and it has nothing to offer.{/trap} {reward}The verse asks what will still be there when everything else leaves.{/reward}
old: The things I rely on will be there when I really need them.
new: Only Allah remains when every other support disappears. He is the one to lean on now.
try: Next time you reach for a comfort habit today, make a short dua first.

title: Never tired of asking, quick to lose hope.
subtitle: How we swing between wanting and despair
then: Ibn Kathir says man {idea}never gets bored of asking for good things{/idea} like wealth and health, but when trial or poverty touches him, he {trap}thinks he will never experience anything good again.{/trap} The verse describes a pattern, not one person.
now: Your duas are long when you want a promotion. Then the rejection email arrives, and you close the prayer mat for a month. {trap}One hard week and you decide nothing will ever go right.{/trap}
old: When something goes wrong, it proves nothing good is coming.
new: Hardship is not the end of good. The same Lord I asked yesterday is there today.
try: If something has gone wrong this week, make one dua for good anyway, today.

title: Relief comes, and he says: I earned this.
subtitle: Taking credit for mercy

row.title: and if there is a Lord
sub: He will be good to me

then: Ibn Kathir says when good comes after difficulty, he says {trap}this is because of me, I deserve this.{/trap} He doubts the Hour, yet assumes if it comes, Allah will treat him well anyway. Ibn Kathir links this to the verse that {trap}man transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.{/trap}
now: The job finally comes through after months of searching. Within a week you are telling people it was your interview skills. {trap}The months of dua are forgotten.{/trap} {reward}It was a taste of mercy.{/reward}
old: When things finally go well, it is because I worked for it.
new: Every relief after hardship is a mercy tasted from Allah, not a wage I earned.
try: Think of one good thing that came after a hard time and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Blessed, he turns away; in trouble, he prays at length.
subtitle: Remembering Allah only in emergencies
then: Ibn Kathir says when given favor, man {trap}turns away from obedience and is too proud.{/trap} When difficulty touches him, he makes long supplications, {trap}long on words, short on meaning.{/trap} He links it to the verse of the man who prays lying, sitting and standing, then forgets once the harm is lifted.
now: In the hospital waiting room you pray like never before. Two weeks after the all-clear, you are back to skipping Fajr. {idea}The verse is not mocking the dua. It is asking you to keep it going.{/idea}
old: I will turn to Allah seriously when I really need Him.
new: I need Him in the good days too. Remembering Him in ease keeps me close in hardship.
try: Make a dua of thanks today for something that is going well right now.

title: What if it really is from Allah?
subtitle: A question worth sitting with
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask the deniers: {idea}tell me, if this Quran is from Allah and you reject it, what is your position?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says such a person is in {trap}stubborn opposition, on a path far from guidance.{/trap}
now: You would not ignore a letter from the bank that says your account is at risk, just in case it is real. {idea}Ask the same honest question about the Quran.{/idea} What if every word is true?
old: I can put off taking the Quran seriously until I am sure.
new: If it is from Allah, then ignoring it is the biggest risk I could take.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: if every verse is true, what one thing would I change?

title: Signs on the horizons and inside yourselves.
subtitle: Proof outside and within, and Allah as Witness
then: Mujahid and others said the signs included events like {idea}Badr and the conquest of Makkah{/idea}, which the Quraysh lived through. Ibn Kathir adds it may mean {idea}the human body and its design{/idea}, showing the Creator's wisdom. And {reward}Allah is enough as a Witness.{/reward}
now: Your heartbeat, without you asking. The way your cut healed by itself. The turn in your life you never planned. {idea}Signs, inside and around you.{/idea} You have been reading them all along without noticing.
old: I would believe more firmly if I saw a clear sign.
new: Signs are already in the world and in my own body. Allah is witness over everything.
try: Put your hand on your chest for a minute today, feel your heartbeat, and say alhamdulillah.

title: In doubt about meeting their Lord, who surrounds everything.
subtitle: The surah ends with the meeting ahead
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}did not think about the Hour or strive for it; they regarded it as irrelevant.{/trap} But it will come. The surah ends saying {idea}all of creation is under His control and knowledge{/idea}, so bringing the Hour is easy for Him.
now: You plan the holiday, the next career step, the kids' schooling. The one meeting that is certain gets no planning at all. {idea}The surah ends by placing it back on your calendar.{/idea}
old: Meeting Allah is far off; I will think about it later.
new: The meeting with my Lord is certain, and He surrounds everything, including my today.
try: Spend two minutes tonight thinking about meeting Allah, and what you hope to bring.
